selection: step-out from bonsai1/L24/N11621- (10x queue, model pilot: haiku)

neighbours.label: verb right after a fronted 'there' or place phrase (existential inversion)
fire: Inside the old barn there was a rusted tractor and some hay.
Beyond the ridge there lies a valley full of wildflowers.
Behind the library there stands a bronze statue of the founder.
At the end of the pier there sits a small wooden bench.
Across the harbor there comes a faint sound of bells.
Along the north wall are hung three faded maps.
Near the station stood the ruins of a brewery.
Beneath the floorboards is hidden a box of letters.
quiet: The old barn has a rusted tractor and some hay.
Is there a faint sound of bells across the harbor?
The statue of the founder stands behind the library.
The small wooden bench sits at the end of the pier.
Im Hafen gibt es ein altes Boot mit blauem Segel.
Three faded maps were hung by the cook on the north wall.
The ruins of a brewery can be seen near the station.
She hid a box of letters beneath the floorboards.

notes: Model pilot (haiku arm; the same pole is tested independently by the other arm, pairing disclosed): this pole feeds the held pole bonsai1/L24/N11621- (zeroing this neuron removes 0.74 of the anchor's peak), from a batched edge measurement with 8 same-layer placebos. Label and all 16 sentences written by the Haiku 5.5 labeller from a packet (card + all-pole band samples + the edge hint) and one probe round of 8 sentences (none reused). An Opus gate checked rule-level items only and edited nothing. Labeller's note: Probe fire sentences scored 0.31 to 0.98 (comes highest, stands borderline), and subject-first, 'has', German 'gibt' and 'is standing' stayed low. The one miss was the yes/no question 'Is there...' at 0.30, which counts as firing at the threshold, so a question near miss is a real edge. The label is about the verb after a fronted place, not the word there.
